title: Employer of Record (EOR) in Ukraine September 2026
body_markdown:
Hiring in Ukraine without registering a local entity is possible for foreign companies, and for most teams it is the right move. This guide covers how an Employer of Record (EOR) works under Ukrainian law, what payroll obligations apply, how costs compare to setting up your own entity, and how Bolto manages the full employment lifecycle in Ukraine: from contract execution and payroll to ongoing compliance. If you are building a distributed team and want a compliant Ukrainian hire in as little as 48 hours, here is what you need to know.


**TLDR:**


- An EOR lets you hire full-time employees in Ukraine without registering a local entity or tracking Labour Code changes yourself.
- Ukrainian payroll carries three obligations: 22% USC (employer), 18% income tax, and 5% military tax (both employee-withheld).
- EOR makes more financial sense than a local entity for teams under 20 hires, where entity fixed costs stay high regardless of headcount.
- Ukraine has 305,000 IT professionals (Ministry of Digital Transformation, 2025), with strong STEM output and EU-compatible time zones that suit European and US teams.
- Bolto handles Ukrainian EOR onboarding in as little as 48 hours, including contracts, payroll setup, and tax registration.


## What Is an Employer of Record in Ukraine


An Employer of Record (EOR) in Ukraine is a third-party company that becomes the legal employer of your Ukrainian staff on paper, while you keep full control over their day-to-day work, role scope, and performance. You direct the work; the EOR owns the legal relationship.


Ukraine applies a strict substance-over-form test when determining who the real employer is. The entity that controls hiring decisions, work direction, discipline, and termination is generally treated as the legal employer under Ukrainian law, regardless of how a contract is structured. Foreign companies that pay someone in Ukraine without proper legal standing typically face serious compliance exposure.


[Employer of Record services](https://www.bolto.com/blog/employer-of-record-services-how-to-choose) operating in Ukraine must register as the legal employer with local tax and social insurance authorities, issue employment contracts in Ukrainian, and run fully compliant payroll including personal income tax (PIT), military tax, and unified social contribution (USC). Without a local entity of your own, an[EOR is the compliant path](https://www.bolto.com/employer-of-record) to hiring full-time employees there.


The structure works like this:


- Your company signs a services agreement with the EOR, defining the scope of work and your management rights over the hire.
- The EOR signs an employment contract directly with your hire, making it the legally registered employer under Ukrainian law.
- The EOR handles contracts, payroll, statutory benefits, and any regulatory changes, so you are not tracking Ukrainian labour law updates yourself.


This is general information, not legal advice. Rules vary by situation and change over time, so consult a qualified employment lawyer for your specific circumstances.


## Employment Laws and Compliance Requirements in Ukraine


Ukraine's Labour Code layers multiple obligations on every employer, and wartime martial law has added a second track of emergency rules that shift with little notice. Getting this wrong as a foreign company is a compliance exposure, not a paperwork gap.


### Payroll Taxes and Employer Social Contributions


Three separate obligations hit every Ukrainian payroll. The employer carries the Unified Social Contribution (USC); personal income tax and military tax are withheld from the employee's gross salary and remitted by the employer.


Obligation Rate Borne By


Unified Social Contribution (USC) 22% of gross salary Employer


Personal Income Tax (PIT) 18% of gross salary Employee (withheld)


Military Tax 5% of gross salary Employee (withheld)


Statutory minimum wage (2026) UAH 8,647/month N/A


The military tax[rate increased to 5%](https://www.accace.com/labour-law-and-employment-in-ukraine/) effective December 2024 under Law No. 4015-IX, up from the prior 1.5%, and remains at 5% through 2026. The USC standard rate remains 22%, capped at UAH 129,705 per employee per month as of 2026 (15× the UAH 8,647 monthly minimum wage) (State Budget Law for 2026, Ukraine, December 2025).


### Leave Entitlements and Working Time


Employees are entitled to 24 days of paid annual leave after six months of service, 126 days of fully paid maternity leave, and parental leave through a child's third birthday. The standard workweek is 40 hours, and overtime is capped at 120 hours per year. Public holidays are fully paid.


### Probation, Termination, and Severance


Probation periods run up to three months. Under Ukraine's Labour Code, termination generally requires documented just cause and written grounds. For economic dismissals, the[minimum notice period is two months](https://cms.law/en/int/expert-guides/cms-expert-guide-to-dismissals/ukraine) , and statutory severance for redundancy is at least one average monthly salary. Protected categories including pregnant employees and parents of children under three have strong dismissal protections that cannot be waived.


Since 2022, wartime emergency measures covering suspensions, notice procedures, and certain HR actions have required active monitoring and application by employers. These rules change frequently under martial law conditions.

Ukrainian LLC incorporation fees can look modest on paper, but the real cost is what comes after: a local accountant, legal counsel for Labour Code compliance, ongoing tax filings, and wartime regulatory monitoring. Those fixed costs stay roughly constant whether you have one Ukrainian employee or twenty, which is the part that catches early-stage teams off guard.


EOR costs scale with headcount. Entity costs largely do not. For companies with one to five Ukrainian hires, or those still testing whether Ukraine is the right fit for their team, that structural difference matters more than any headline incorporation figure. ## EOR vs. Local Entity in Ukraine: Which Is Right for You


When EOR makes sense in Ukraine depends mostly on your headcount and timeline.[The best EOR for startups](https://www.bolto.com/blog/what-is-the-best-eor-for-startups) is the right structure when you're making one to several hires and haven't committed to Ukraine long term. It's also the practical choice when wartime legislative conditions create compliance uncertainty you don't want to track internally, when you need someone active in 48 hours and can't afford to wait weeks for entity registration, or when you want to test Ukraine's talent market before deciding whether a permanent presence is worth building.


### When a Local Entity Becomes Worth Considering


At roughly 20 or more employees, the per-seat EOR cost can exceed what it costs to maintain a local legal entity. Reviewing the[best global EOR providers for startups](https://www.bolto.com/blog/best-global-eor-providers-for-startups) can help you benchmark pricing before that threshold. If you're also administering equity directly for Ukrainian staff, or you have committed local leadership and a long-term market presence, the entity structure gives you more control. One cost to factor in upfront: entity exit in Ukraine requires a formal liquidation process that typically takes several months and needs local legal support. If you later need to[change employer of record providers](https://www.bolto.com/blog/how-to-change-employer-of-record-step-by-step) , that transition has its own steps worth understanding early. That exit burden is a real line item in any entity decision, not a procedural footnote.


For companies still in the one-to-ten hire range, or testing whether Ukraine fits their hiring strategy, EOR removes the setup cost, the compliance overhead, and the exit risk entirely.


## Final Thoughts


Ukraine has a strong technical talent pool, competitive salaries, and EU-compatible time zones. These three factors keep drawing foreign companies to build teams there despite ongoing wartime conditions. For most companies in the early stages of hiring in Ukraine, an EOR removes the setup cost, the compliance overhead, and the exit risk that come with running a local entity. ## FAQs


### What does an employer of record in Ukraine actually handle, and what do you still control?


With an employer of record in Ukraine, the EOR becomes the legal employer on paper: it issues Ukrainian-language contracts, runs payroll in hryvnia, remits USC at 22%, withholds personal income tax and military tax, and manages statutory benefits and compliance filings. You retain full control over day-to-day direction, performance management, role scope, and what your employee builds or delivers.


### Can I hire in Ukraine without setting up a local entity?


Yes. An employer of record in Ukraine lets you bring on full-time employees without forming a local LLC or registering with Ukrainian authorities yourself. The EOR holds the legal entity and handles all tax and labor law obligations, so you can have a payroll-ready hire in as little as 48 hours instead of waiting weeks for entity registration.


### Employer of record Ukraine vs. local entity: which makes more financial sense for a small team?


For one to five hires, an EOR is almost always the better economics. Entity costs in Ukraine are largely fixed regardless of headcount: you still pay a local accountant, legal counsel for Labour Code compliance, and ongoing wartime regulatory monitoring whether you have one employee or twenty. EOR costs scale with headcount, so the per-seat model fits early-stage teams far better. See the EOR vs. Local Entity section above for a full cost breakdown.


### How does Ukraine's military tax affect employer of record payroll calculations?


The military tax rate increased to 5% of gross salary in late 2024 under Law No. 4015-IX, up from the prior 1.5%. It is withheld from the employee's gross salary and remitted by the employer each payroll cycle, alongside the 18% personal income tax withholding and the employer-side USC at 22%. When using Bolto's EOR service, all three obligations are calculated and filed automatically, and you can use the pre-hire cost calculator to see the full employer cost breakdown before making an offer.


### What hiring risks should I factor in when building a team in Ukraine right now?


Two factors stand out. First, wartime martial law continues to layer emergency measures on top of the standard Labour Code, and these rules change with little notice, so real-time compliance monitoring is not optional. Second, mobilization risk for male candidates is a genuine market factor worth raising with local recruiting specialists early when building your sourcing plan, and not something to treat as an afterthought after you've identified candidates.
